questions.title: Section A - Multiple Choice, Terminology, Matching, Blood Group Pedigree and Protein Synthesis

subQuestions.questionText:
The base pairing in DNA was discovered by …
A) Watson and Wilkins.
B) Franklin and Wilkins.
C) Franklin and Crick.
D) Crick and Watson.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (2 marks)
The complementary base pairing in DNA (A-T, C-G) is part of the Watson-Crick model of DNA structure.

subQuestions.questionText:
A gene codes for the production of …
A) a chromosome.
B) an allele.
C) DNA.
D) a protein.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (2 marks)
A gene is a sequence of DNA that codes for the production of a specific protein (polypeptide).

subQuestions.questionText:
Which ONE of the following is a characteristic of stem cells?
A) They are easily obtained from any organ.
B) They divide by meiosis.
C) They are haploid.
D) They can be stimulated to form any type of cell needed.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (2 marks)
Stem cells are undifferentiated cells that can be stimulated to develop into any type of specialised cell needed.

options.A: They are easily obtained from any organ.
options.D: They can be stimulated to form any type of cell needed.

subQuestions.questionText:
The chances of having a female child in humans is …
A) 25%
B) 50%
C) 75%
D) 100%
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (2 marks)
Sex is determined by the sperm (X or Y); there is a 50% chance of an XX (female) combination.

subQuestions.questionText:
Which ONE of the following is part of the reason why colour-blindness is more common in males than in females?
A) The allele for colour-blindness is recessive and located on the X-chromosome.
B) Colour-blind males have two copies of the allele for colour-blindness.
C) The allele for colour-blindness is recessive and located on the Y-chromosome.
D) Fathers pass the allele of colour-blindness to their sons only.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A (2 marks)
The colour-blindness allele is recessive and carried on the X-chromosome, so a male (XY) with only one recessive allele will express the trait.

options.A: The allele for colour-blindness is recessive and located on the X-chromosome.
options.B: Colour-blind males have two copies of the allele for colour-blindness.
options.C: The allele for colour-blindness is recessive and located on the Y-chromosome.
options.D: Fathers pass the allele of colour-blindness to their sons only.

subQuestions.questionText:
The DNA profiles of four individuals (W, X, Y and Z) are given in the question paper. Which individuals are possible members of the same family?
A) X and Z only
B) X, Y and Z only
C) W, Y and Z only
D) W, X and Y only
(Refer to the diagram in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (2 marks)
Based on the DNA profiles shown, W, Y and Z share matching band patterns, indicating they are possible members of the same family.

subQuestions.questionText:
When two plants heterozygous for a characteristic are crossed, the expected ratio (dominant phenotype : recessive phenotype) is:
A) 3 : 1
B) 1 : 3
C) 1 : 2
D) 1 : 1
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A (2 marks)
A monohybrid cross between two heterozygotes gives a 3:1 dominant to recessive phenotypic ratio.

subQuestions.questionText:
The diagram in the question paper represents the structure of chromosomes (Q, R, S and T) at different stages of meiotic cell division. Which ONE of the following chromosomes would be found in a cell during late Anaphase II?
A) Q
B) R
C) S
D) T
(Refer to the diagram in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (2 marks)
Chromosome S represents the single (unpaired) chromatid structure found in a cell during late Anaphase II.

subQuestions.questionText:
The scientist who discovered Little Foot is …
A) Lee Berger.
B) Raymond Dart.
C) Ron Clarke.
D) Robert Broom.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (2 marks)
Ron Clarke discovered the near-complete Australopithecus skeleton known as 'Little Foot' at Sterkfontein.

subQuestions.questionText: Give the correct biological term for the following description: The position of a gene on a chromosome.
subQuestions.memoText: Locus (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give the correct biological term for the following description: The type of evolution characterised by long periods of little or no change followed by short periods of rapid change.
subQuestions.memoText: Punctuated equilibrium (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give the correct biological term for the following description: The natural shape of a DNA molecule.
subQuestions.memoText: Double helix (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give the correct biological term for the following description: The type of bond found between two amino acids.
subQuestions.memoText: Peptide bond (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give the correct biological term for the following description: The type of vision shared in primates that allows for depth perception.
subQuestions.memoText: Stereoscopic / binocular vision (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give the correct biological term for the following description: The type of dominance which results in an intermediate phenotype in the heterozygous condition.
subQuestions.memoText: Incomplete dominance (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give the correct biological term for the following description: The fluid of the nucleus where free nucleotides are found.
subQuestions.memoText: Nucleoplasm (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give the correct biological term for the following description: A tangled mass of chromosomes located within the nucleus.
subQuestions.memoText: Chromatin network (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give the correct biological term for the following description: The division of the cytoplasm after a nuclear division.
subQuestions.memoText: Cytokinesis (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give the correct biological term for the following description: The name for the X and Y sex chromosomes in humans.
subQuestions.memoText: Gonosomes (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Indicate whether the description applies to A ONLY, B ONLY, BOTH A AND B or NONE of the items in COLUMN II.
Description (COLUMN I): A genetic disorder caused by a chromosomal mutation.
A: Haemophilia
B: Colour-blindness
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: None (2 marks)
Both haemophilia and colour-blindness are caused by gene mutations (recessive sex-linked alleles), not by chromosomal mutations.

subQuestions.questionText:
Indicate whether the description applies to A ONLY, B ONLY, BOTH A AND B or NONE of the items in COLUMN II.
Description (COLUMN I): The importance of meiosis.
A: Formation of gametes
B: Halving of the chromosome number
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: Both A and B (2 marks)
Meiosis is important for the formation of gametes AND for halving the chromosome number so that the diploid number is restored at fertilisation.

subQuestions.questionText:
Indicate whether the description applies to A ONLY, B ONLY, BOTH A AND B or NONE of the items in COLUMN II.
Description (COLUMN I): The organelle where DNA is found in plants.
A: Mitochondria
B: Chloroplast
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: Both A and B (2 marks)
In plant cells DNA is found in both the mitochondria and the chloroplasts (as well as the nucleus).

questions.title: Section B - Meiosis, DNA Replication, Mutations (VKORC1), Genetic Crosses and Dihybrid Inheritance

subQuestions.questionText:
The diagrams in the question paper (Diagram 1 and Diagram 2) represent two stages of meiotic cell division, with structures labelled A, B, C and D.
Name structure:
(a) B
(b) C
(Refer to the diagram in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) B — Centriole/centrosome (1 mark)
(b) C — Spindle fibre (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Refer to the meiosis diagrams in the question paper. Identify the phase represented in Diagram 1.
(Refer to the diagram in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText: Prophase I (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Give THREE reasons for your answer to QUESTION 2.1.2.
(Refer to the diagram in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Any THREE of the following (Mark first THREE only) (3 marks):
- Pairing of homologous chromosomes is visible/bivalents are visible
- Development of spindle fibres
- Crossing over is taking place
- Centriole/centrosome moved to opposite poles
- Disintegration of the nuclear membrane

subQuestions.questionText:
Describe the process taking place at A.
(Refer to the diagram in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
(3 marks):
- Parts of the homologous chromosomes overlap and
- DNA/genetic material is exchanged
- at points called chiasmata/chiasma

subQuestions.questionText:
(a) Identify the phase represented in Diagram 2.
(b) Describe the difference in the events that take place in the phase mentioned in (a) and the same phase during mitosis.
(Refer to the diagram in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) Metaphase I (1 mark)

(b) (2 marks):
- In Metaphase I/Meiosis I chromosomes are arranged in pairs at the equator
- In mitosis the chromosomes are arranged singly at the equator

subQuestions.questionText:
Describe the results at the end of meiosis if the chromosomes at D failed to separate.
(Refer to the diagram in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
(3 marks):
- Four (daughter) cells will be formed of which
- two will each have five chromosomes and
- the other two will each have three chromosomes

subQuestions.questionText: Describe the process of DNA replication.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any SIX of the following (6 marks):
- The (DNA) double helix unwinds and
- unzips/hydrogen bonds break
- to form two separate strands
- Both (DNA) strands serve as templates
- to build a complementary (DNA) strand/A pairs with T and C pairs with G
- using free (DNA) nucleotides from the nucleoplasm
- This results in two identical (DNA) molecules

subQuestions.questionText:
Read the information below.
A gene, VKORC1, codes for a blood-clotting factor in humans. This gene is made up of 163 amino acids. A mutation occurred that affected amino acid 128 and 139: the sequence CTG changed to CAG and the TAT became TCT. This mutation has been transmitted as an autosomal dominant characteristic through the generations. The mutation has resulted in resistance to Warfarin drugs in humans. Warfarin is used in the treatment of thrombosis. Thrombosis results in the formation of a blood clot in the artery. Warfarin causes the thinning of blood to break down the blood clot.

Give ONE piece of evidence from the information that shows that the mutation for this gene occurred in the DNA molecule.
subQuestions.memoText: The presence of T/thymine in the original sequence (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Refer to the information about the VKORC1 gene. How many nitrogenous bases code for the VKORC1 gene?
subQuestions.memoText:
489 (2 marks)
[163 amino acids x 3 bases per codon = 489 nitrogenous bases.]

subQuestions.questionText: Describe what is meant by an autosomal dominant allele.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any THREE of the following (3 marks):
- A form of a gene
- that is carried on chromosome 1 to 22 and
- is always expressed in the phenotype of an individual
- in the heterozygous condition

subQuestions.questionText:
The table below shows the amino acids and their corresponding codons.
CODON — AMINO ACID
GAC — Leu
UCU — Ser
AUA — Try
GUC — Gln
AGA — Arg
ACA — Trp
CAG — Gln
UAU — Phe

Explain:
(a) How the mutation on the VKORC1 gene resulted in resistance to Warfarin in humans
(b) The effect of this mutation on humans with thrombosis
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) Any FIVE of the following (5 marks):
- The codon changed from GAC to GUC
- resulting in amino acid Leu replaced by Gln
- The other codon changed from AUA to AGA
- resulting in amino acid Try replaced by Arg
- This changed the sequence of amino acids
- A different protein was formed

(b) (3 marks):
- Harmful effect
- The blood clot is not broken down
- Leading to blockage of arteries/oxygen and nutrients are not transported to cells

subQuestions.questionText: Polydactyly is a condition that leads to extra fingers or toes. It is caused by a dominant allele. A man who is heterozygous for polydactyly has a wife who is not polydactyl. Using the letters R and r, do a genetic cross to show the percentage chance that their children will have polydactyly.
subQuestions.memoText:
1 COMPULSORY mark + Any 5 (Total 6 marks):

P1 Phenotype: With polydactyly x Without polydactyly
Genotype: Rr x rr
[Meiosis]
Gametes: R, r x r, r
[Fertilisation]
F1 Genotype: Rr, Rr, rr, rr
F1 Phenotype: 2 polydactyly ; 2 without polydactyly
50% chance of polydactyl child (compulsory mark)

Mark allocation: P1 phenotype and genotype, Meiosis and Fertilisation labels, gametes, F1 genotype/phenotype = any 5; the 50% chance = 1 compulsory mark.

OR (Punnett square layout):
P1 Phenotype: With polydactyly x Without polydactyly
Genotype: Rr x rr
Gametes:  R | r
  r  → Rr | rr
  r  → Rr | rr
(1 mark for correct gametes; 1 mark for correct genotypes)
F1 Phenotype: 2 polydactyly ; 2 without polydactyly
50% chance of polydactyl child (1 compulsory mark + any 5).

subQuestions.questionText:
In summer squash plants, white fruit colour (B) is dominant over yellow fruit colour (b), and round fruit (D) is dominant over oval fruit (d). A summer squash plant that is homozygous for white and round fruit is crossed with a plant that is homozygous for yellow and oval fruit.
State the:
(a) Genotypes of the P1-parents
(b) Phenotypes of the F1-generation
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) BBDD and bbdd (2 marks)
(b) White, round fruit (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText:
Refer to the summer squash cross (white fruit B dominant over yellow b; round fruit D dominant over oval d). Two plants that are heterozygous for both characteristics were crossed.
(a) Give ALL the possible genotypes in the gametes that will be formed.
(b) How many plants in the next generation are likely to have yellow and oval fruit?
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) BD, bD, Bd, bd (2 marks)
(b) One/1 (1 mark)
[A BbDd x BbDd cross gives a 9:3:3:1 ratio, so 1 out of 16 plants is expected to have yellow and oval (bbdd) fruit.]

subQuestions.questionText: Refer to the summer squash cross (white fruit B dominant over yellow b; round fruit D dominant over oval d). Give the possible genotypes of both parents that must be crossed if a farmer wants summer squash that are white with oval fruit only.
subQuestions.memoText:
BBdd and BBdd
OR
BBdd and Bbdd
OR
BBdd and bbdd
(2 marks)

questions.title: Section B - Artificial and Natural Selection, Lizard Investigation and Human Evolution

subQuestions.questionText:
The graph in the question paper shows the results of artificial selection for protein content in mealie plants over 50 generations (x-axis: generations of mealie plants, 0 to 50; y-axis: average percentage protein content in mealie grains/kernels).
Describe how this farmer did artificial selection of the mealie plant.
(Refer to the diagram in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
(3 marks):
- The farmer interbred
- mealie plants with a high protein content
- over 50/many generations

subQuestions.questionText:
Refer to the artificial selection graph in the question paper. What was the average percentage of the protein content in the mealie grains (kernels) at the 15th generation?
(Refer to the diagram in the question paper.)

Refer to the artificial selection graph in the question paper. By how many times did the average percentage of the protein content in the mealie grains (kernels) increase between the 40th and 50th generation? Show ALL working.
(Refer to the diagram in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText: 20 / 14 = 1,43 times (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Describe ONE way in which the process of artificial selection is different from genetic engineering.
subQuestions.memoText:
(Mark first ONE only) (2 marks):
- Artificial selection: organisms with a desired characteristic are interbred
- Genetic engineering: genes coding for the desired characteristic are inserted into an organism

subQuestions.questionText: Describe Darwin's theory of evolution by natural selection.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any SEVEN of the following (7 marks):
- There is variation amongst the offspring in a population
- Some have favourable characteristics and some do not
- When there is a change in the environmental conditions/there is competition
- organisms with a favourable characteristic survive
- whilst organisms with an unfavourable characteristic die
- The organisms that survive, reproduce
- and pass on the allele for the favourable characteristic to their offspring
- The next generation will therefore have a higher proportion of individuals with the favourable characteristic

subQuestions.questionText:
An investigation was done to determine the relationship between the height of the head and bite force in lizards. The procedure was as follows:
- The scientists collected 120 lizards with similar characteristics that were around the same reproductive age in different habitats.
- Their body characteristics and DNA were analysed to determine if they belonged to the same species.
- 40 lizards belonged to species A, 36 to species B and 44 to species C.
- Each species was kept in its cage with environmental conditions similar to their habitats.
- The height of the head was measured for each lizard and averages calculated for each species.
- Using a Kistler force, the bite force of each lizard in each species was measured five times and the average calculated for each lizard and each species.
The results are shown in the table below.
Species | Height of the head (mm) | Bite force (N)
A | 10,3 | 12,4
B | 10,7 | 14,3
C | 13,2 | 20,4

Identify the:
(a) Independent variable
(b) Dependent variable
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) Height of the head (1 mark)
(b) Bite force (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Refer to the lizard investigation described in the question paper. State TWO factors that were kept constant for this investigation.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO of the following (Mark first TWO only) (2 marks):
- Similar characteristics
- (Same) reproductive age
- (Same) measuring tool/Kistler force used to measure bite force
- Each species kept in environmental conditions similar to their habitats
- Lizards of the same species in each group

subQuestions.questionText: Refer to the lizard investigation described in the question paper. Apart from the sample size, state ONE way in which the reliability of the results was ensured for this investigation.
subQuestions.memoText: Five measurements of the bite force (Mark first ONE only) (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Refer to the lizard investigation described in the question paper. The height of the head was different in each species of lizard. Name the type of variation displayed by this characteristic.
subQuestions.memoText: Continuous variation (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Refer to the lizard investigation data in the question paper. Describe the relationship between the height of the head of the lizards and the bite force.
subQuestions.memoText:

Lizards with an increased head height have a stronger bite force
OR

Refer to the hominid skulls in the question paper. Explain the significance of the change in prognathism from A. sediba to H. sapiens.
